chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abu Abdullah al-Razi, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Al-Hakam ibn Maskin, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) say:
Eating soap weakens the knees and spoils the semen.

key_terms.الْأَشْنَانِ: Soap (specifically referring to a type of soap or detergent in classical context)

ai.seo_question: What are the physical effects of eating soap according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) medical wisdom linking the consumption of soap (*al-ashnan*) to specific physical ailments, notably weakening the knees and impairing semen quality. This narration reflects the Shia tradition of integrating practical health advice with spiritual and physical well-being, emphasizing how dietary habits directly influence bodily vitality and reproductive health.
